words: フォームを作成します

article_text_en.welcome: Formalie helps your organisation collect information with forms, review what comes in and send it where it is needed: a database, another system through the API, or a report. The Forms page: your responses at a glance at the top, your forms below. The main parts Forms: build forms, share them and follow their responses. Data sources: connect your own databases to store responses and explore them. API service: let other systems read and send data through your own endpoints. AI assistant: create forms, analyse answers and translate with help. People: invite your team and decide what each person may do. Press Ctrl + K (or ⌘ + K on a Mac) anywhere to search for a page, a form or a setting. Open your forms
article_text_en.find-your-way: The narrow column on the far left is the rail. Each icon opens an area of Formalie: Forms, Data sources, API service, AI assistant and People. The menu next to it changes with the area you are in. The rail and the area's menu. On phones and tablets they open from the menu button at the top left. At the top of every page you find its title, where you are (the breadcrumbs) and the page’s buttons. The main button is always the dark one on the right. Collapse the menu with the « button or the [ key to get more room. Dark mode is at the bottom of the menu, under System. Help & support is at the foot of the rail and in the System group. On a phone, the menu opens from the ☰ button at the top left.
article_text_en.first-form: You can start a form in three ways: from a blank page, from one of Formalie’s templates, or by describing it to the AI assistant. New form: start blank, from a template or by importing a form file. Click New form at the top right of the Forms page. Choose Blank, pick a template, or import a form file. Give the form a name and, if you like, a folder. The builder opens: add questions from the field list on the left. When you are happy, click Publish and share the link. Not sure where to start? The AI assistant can draft the whole form from a few words: open AI assistant → Create a form. Start a new form
article_text_en.invite-your-team: Everyone in your workspace has a profile with their department, job title and role. The role decides what they can see and do. People: everyone in your workspace, with Add user and Sign-up links at the top. Open People from the rail. Click Add user to create a profile: the person gets an email to set their password. Or open Sign-up links to share a link: people who sign up with it wait for your approval. Open People
article_text_en.keyboard-and-search: Search opens with Ctrl + K (⌘ + K on a Mac). Type part of a page, form, setting or person and press Enter. Every keyboard shortcut, in Help & support → Keyboard shortcuts. Press ? to see every keyboard shortcut. Many pages add their own, for example J and K to move between responses in a panel. Every list and panel works with the keyboard alone: Tab moves, Enter opens, Esc closes.
article_text_en.forms-list: The Forms page lists every form you may see. The two cards at the top show recent responses and how your forms are spread across draft, published and closed; click a status in the legend to show only those forms. Forms as cards, with search, filters and the Table / Grid switch. Search by name, tag or owner. Filter by status, folder, owner or tag; filters show as chips you can clear. Columns lets you show, hide and reorder the table’s columns. Table / Grid switches between rows and cards; Formalie remembers your choice. Right-click a form, or use its ⋯ menu, for actions such as duplicate, move or archive. Open the forms list
article_text_en.form-lifecycle: Draft: being built; nobody can fill it in yet. Published: open for responses at its link. Closed: the link still works but shows that the form is closed; no new responses. Archived: put away; hidden from the main list, responses kept. A published form can have unpublished changes: your edits stay in the draft until you publish again, so respondents never see a half-finished change. Forms filtered to Published: click a status in the card at the top to filter. Set opening and closing dates in Share → Availability so a form opens and closes by itself.
article_text_en.folders: Folders group forms, for example by team or project. Create one with + next to Folders in the menu, then move forms into it from their ⋯ menu. Folders, with the number of forms and responses in each. Admins can limit a folder to some roles, departments or people with Folder access. Everyone else doesn’t see the folder, its forms or their responses anywhere, not even in search or exports.
article_text_en.trash: When you delete a form it goes to Trash for 30 days, with its responses. You can restore it from there at any time in those 30 days. Trash: deleted forms stay here for 30 days. Delete forever in the trash removes the form and all its responses for good. It can’t be undone. Open the trash
article_text_en.builder-basics: The builder has three parts: the field list on the left, the form in the middle and the settings of what you selected on the right. The builder: the field list, the form and the settings of what you selected. Drag a field from the list onto the form, or click it to add it after the selected field. Click a field to change its question, help text, whether it’s required, and more. Put fields side by side by dropping them next to each other; use Width to size them. Add pages with Add page to split a long form. Your changes save as you work; Undo and Redo are at the top. No mouse? Select a field and use Alt + ↑ / ↓ to move it, Ctrl + D to duplicate and Delete to remove. The Assistant button in the builder suggests missing questions, writes help texts and checks your form.
article_text_en.field-types: Text: short and long answers, email, phone, number, amount, full name. Dates: date, time, date and time, date range, duration. Choices: dropdown, radio, checkboxes, yes / no, ranking, matrix, agreement. Ratings: stars, a 0 to 10 scale, a slider. Files: file upload, photo upload, signature. Location: address, country, language, time zone. Advanced: hidden values and calculations. Layout: section headings, text, images and dividers. Pick the most specific field: an email field checks the address as people type, a date field shows a calendar, a phone field checks the number. The field list groups every kind of question: text, dates, choices, ratings, files and more. Long lists of choices (countries, departments) work best as a List Option, kept once and used in many forms.
article_text_en.builder-logic: Logic rules change the form while people fill it in: show a follow-up only after a yes, require a phone number for urgent requests, or jump to the end. The Logic tab: each rule says When something is answered, Then what happens. Open the Logic tab of the form. Click Add rule and choose When: a question, a condition and a value. Choose Then: show, hide, require, set a value or jump to a page. Add more conditions with and / or if needed. A question that a rule hides is never required, so people can always send the form.
article_text_en.calculations: A Calculation field works out a value from other answers, for example quantity × price, an average rating or a risk score. People see the result as they fill in the form. A form in the builder; a Calculation field works out its value from other answers. Write the formula with the questions’ keys in braces, for example {quantity} * {unit_price}. Choices can carry a score so they can be added up.
article_text_en.publish-and-versions: Publish makes your draft the live form. Each publish is saved as a numbered version with an optional note about what changed. Versions: every publish, ready to compare or restore. In Versions you can compare any version with the draft and restore an older one into the draft. The Publish button is greyed out when there is nothing new to publish.
article_text_en.design-a-form: Open the Design tab of a form to change its look. The preview shows the form as people will see it, on a computer, tablet or phone. The Design tab with the live preview. Start from a ready starting point, then adjust. Change colours, fonts, the size of fields and buttons. Add your logo, a cover image or a coloured band at the top. Design the thank-you page people see after sending. Save a design as a theme to use it on other forms in one click.
article_text_en.themes: Themes are saved designs. Formalie ships a set; your workspace can add its own from the designer, or let the AI assistant suggest designs from your brand colour. Themes: Formalie’s designs and your workspace’s own. Choose the theme new forms start with in Settings → Form defaults. Open themes
article_text_en.landing-pages: A landing page is the page your form sits on: a banner with the title, an introduction, how long it takes and your organisation. Pick one in the designer or keep your own in Landing pages. Landing pages: the page a form sits on.
article_text_en.use-a-template: The template gallery has ready forms for HR, health and safety, events, sales and more. Each one comes with its questions, logic, calculations and a matching design. The template gallery, by category. Open Templates from the menu. Browse by category or search. Open a template to try it in the preview. Click Use template: a new draft form opens in the builder. Browse templates
article_text_en.save-as-template: Any form can become a template for your workspace: open its ⋯ menu and choose Save as template. Give it a name, a description and a category. Your templates appear under Your templates. Your templates appear in the gallery next to Formalie’s.
article_text_en.share-a-form: Open the Share tab of a published form. From there you can copy its link, download a QR code, create a short link or send email invitations. The Share tab: where people can answer and who can open the form. Link: copy it and paste it anywhere. Custom link: choose a readable address. QR code: for posters and printed material. Invitations: email people a personal link and see who has responded. Open your forms
article_text_en.who-can-fill-in: Anyone with the link. With a password you give out. Invite only: only people you invited by email. Your organisation: people signed in to your workspace. In Availability you can open and close the form on set dates and stop it after a number of responses. Who can fill in the form and when, in its Share settings.
article_text_en.embed-a-form: In Share → Embed copy the code and paste it into your website. You can limit which websites may show the form. Embedding and allowed websites are in the Share tab too.
article_text_en.form-languages: A form has a main language and can offer more. In the builder, open the form settings, add a language under More languages and translate each text side by side. Form settings in the builder, where you add more languages. Translate the rest with AI fills in what is still to do; you check every text before publishing.
article_text_en.responses-basics: Responses lists your forms with their responses. Open a form to see its responses as a table or as cards; open a response to see every answer in a panel. A form’s responses, with the cards at the top and the list below. Use J and K to move to the next or previous response. Filter by status, date, channel or answer. Insights shows a summary per question: choices, averages and the latest text answers. Open responses
article_text_en.review-responses: Each response has a status: New, Reviewed, Approved or Rejected. Change it with one click at the top of the response panel. A response open in its panel: the status bar at the top, tags and notes below. Add tags and notes to keep track. Correcting answers is a separate permission, so your role may let you review without changing what people wrote.
article_text_en.export-responses: Click Export on a form’s responses, choose the format and what to include. Large exports are prepared in the background; you see their progress in Exports and get a message when the file is ready. Exports: files being prepared and ready to download.
article_text_en.analytics: Analytics shows how many people opened, started and completed each form, how long it takes and where people stop. Open a form to see each page and question. Analytics: views, starts, completions and where people stop. A question where many people stop is often unclear or asks too much. Try a shorter question or make it optional.
article_text_en.lists-basics: A List Option holds choices you use in many forms, for example departments, products or countries. Change the list once and every form that uses it follows. List Option: lists of choices used in many forms. Lists can have levels: pick a country, then only its regions show, then its cities. Very large lists stay on the server and load as people type. Lists marked Formalie are provided for every workspace; you can use them but not change them.
article_text_en.data-sources-basics: Data sources connects Formalie to your own databases. Responses can then be stored there too, in tables Formalie creates and keeps in step with the form. Connections to your databases, with their health. Open Data sources from the rail and click Add connection. Choose the database type and enter its details; Test now checks it works. In a form’s Response storage, choose the connection: new responses are stored there. Give Formalie a database user with only the rights it needs.
article_text_en.database-explorer: The Database explorer shows the tables of a connection and their rows. The Query editor runs SQL; statements that change data need their own permission and ask first. The Database explorer: tables on the left, their rows on the right.
article_text_en.api-basics: The API service gives other systems their own endpoints: read responses, send new ones, or look up list options. Each service groups endpoints and has its own documentation page. API services, each with its endpoints and documentation. Open API service and create a service. Add endpoints for the forms or data you want to offer. Create a token for the system that will call it. Try the endpoint from the documentation page.
article_text_en.api-tokens: Each system that calls your API gets a token. Tokens can expire and be revoked at any time. Access rules limit addresses, times and how many calls are allowed. Tokens & headers: the keys systems use to call your API. A token is shown once. Keep it in a safe place and never put it in a public web page.
article_text_en.webhooks: A webhook sends a message to another system’s address when something happens, for example a new response. Formalie retries failed deliveries and shows each delivery so you can see what was sent. Webhooks and their deliveries.
article_text_en.roles-and-access: Every person has one role. Owner can do everything; Admin and Member are ready to use and can be changed; you can add your own roles. Roles & access: each role and who holds it. Each action has a reach: None, Own (what they made), Shared (forms shared with them), Own & shared or All. For example, a role may see all responses but only change its own forms. Open Roles & access
article_text_en.sign-up-links: A sign-up link lets people create their own account. You can limit it to your organisation’s email addresses. Their accounts wait in Awaiting approval until an admin approves them and gives them a role. Sign-up links are at the top of People; approvals wait in Awaiting approval.
article_text_en.your-profile: Open your profile from your name at the bottom of the menu. Change your photo, name, language, time zone and date format, your password and your two-step sign-in, and see where you are signed in. Your profile: photo, name, language, password and sign-in.
article_text_en.two-step-sign-in: Two-step sign-in asks for a code after your password. Set up an authenticator app in your profile for the safest option, and keep the recovery codes somewhere safe. Two-step sign-in is set up in your profile.
article_text_en.workspace-settings: Settings holds what applies to the whole workspace: company details, branding, language and region, appearance, sign-in, security, notifications, email templates, privacy and form defaults. Settings: everything that applies to the whole workspace. Open settings
article_text_en.security-settings: In Settings → Security admins set password rules, require two-step sign-in, decide how long people stay signed in and, if needed, allow sign-in only from your networks. Settings → Security. Before limiting networks, add your own address, or you may lock yourself out.
article_text_en.form-defaults: Form defaults sets the theme, progress bar, labels, thank-you message and emails every new form starts with. Forms you already have don’t change. Settings → Form defaults.
article_text_en.audit-trail: The Audit trail records every action in your workspace: sign-ins, changes to forms, responses, settings, people and more, with who did it, when and from where. The audit trail: who did what, when and from where. Filter by area, person or date and open an entry to see what changed. You can export the trail if your role allows it. Open the audit trail
article_text_en.ai-overview: The AI assistant creates forms and templates, helps in the builder, analyses responses and translates. It always proposes: nothing is created, changed or sent until you choose to. The AI assistant’s overview: credits, what it can do and the latest requests. Every request is kept in History with what came back. Each request uses credits from your monthly allowance. Admins choose what it may read and can switch it off. Open the AI assistant
article_text_en.ai-create-form: Create a form: describe it on the left, the draft and its preview on the right. Open AI assistant → Create a form. Describe the form, for example “a visitor sign-in with name, company and arrival time”, or paste a paper form. Click Generate and check the preview. Create form opens it in the builder; Try again gives another take. List what you want to ask, separated by commas: the assistant keeps your words.
article_text_en.ai-analysis: In Response analysis, pick a form and a period. The assistant finds what written answers are about, their tone, and how ratings and choices changed. Response analysis: pick a form and a period, then ask questions below. Ask questions in plain words, like “How many responses last month?”. The answer always shows what was counted.
article_text_en.ai-translate: Translations translates a form into any of the 20 languages; you check each text side by side before saving. Rewrite suggests plainer wording in the tone you choose and shows the reading age before and after. Translations: pick a form and languages, then check each text side by side.
article_text_en.ai-settings: Admins switch the assistant on or off, choose what it may read (forms, responses, data sources), keep personal data out and choose how long requests are kept. The assistant never trains on your data. AI settings: on or off, what it may read, privacy and usage.

items: Нажмите **Новая форма** в правом верхнем углу страницы «Формы».

items: اضغط **نموذج جديد** أعلى صفحة النماذج.
اختر **فارغ**، أو اختر **قالبًا**، أو **استورد** ملف نموذج.
امنح النموذج اسمًا، ومجلدًا إن رغبت.
يُفتح المُنشئ: أضف الأسئلة من قائمة الحقول على الجانب.
عندما ترضى عن النتيجة، اضغط **نشر** وشارك الرابط.

answers_for.q: how do I create a form

blocks.text: افتح تبويب **مشاركة** في نموذج منشور. ومنه يمكنك نسخ رابطه وتنزيل رمز QR وإنشاء رابط مختصر أو إرسال دعوات بالبريد الإلكتروني.

answers_for.q: how do I create a form

blocks.text: عند حذف نموذج ينتقل إلى **سلة المهملات** 30 يومًا مع ردوده. ويمكنك استعادته من هناك في أي وقت خلال هذه الأيام الـ 30.

answers_for.q: how do I create a form

blocks.text: السمات هي تصاميم محفوظة. تأتي Formalie بمجموعة منها؛ ويمكن لمساحة عملك إضافة سماتها من المصمّم، أو أن يقترح مساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي تصاميم من لون علامتك.

welcome.title: Welcome to Formalie
welcome.summary: What Formalie does and how the portal is laid out.

blocks.text: Formalie helps your organisation collect information with forms, review what comes in and send it where it is needed: a database, another system through the API, or a report.

blocks.caption: The Forms page: your responses at a glance at the top, your forms below.

blocks.text: The main parts

items: **Forms**: build forms, share them and follow their responses.
**Data sources**: connect your own databases to store responses and explore them.
**API service**: let other systems read and send data through your own endpoints.
**AI assistant**: create forms, analyse answers and translate with help.
**People**: invite your team and decide what each person may do.

blocks.text: Press **Ctrl + K** (or **⌘ + K** on a Mac) anywhere to search for a page, a form or a setting.

find-your-way.title: Find your way around
find-your-way.summary: The rail, the menu, the header and the search.

blocks.text: The narrow column on the far left is the **rail**. Each icon opens an area of Formalie: Forms, Data sources, API service, AI assistant and People. The menu next to it changes with the area you are in.

blocks.caption: The rail and the area's menu. On phones and tablets they open from the menu button at the top left.

blocks.text: At the top of every page you find its title, where you are (the breadcrumbs) and the page’s buttons. The main button is always the dark one on the right.

items: **Collapse the menu** with the « button or the **[** key to get more room.
**Dark mode** is at the bottom of the menu, under System.
**Help & support** is at the foot of the rail and in the System group.

blocks.text: On a phone, the menu opens from the ☰ button at the top left.

first-form.title: Create your first form
first-form.summary: From a blank page, a template or a description, in a few minutes.

blocks.text: You can start a form in three ways: from a blank page, from one of Formalie’s templates, or by describing it to the AI assistant.

blocks.caption: New form: start blank, from a template or by importing a form file.

items: Click **New form** at the top right of the Forms page.
Choose **Blank**, pick a **template**, or **import** a form file.
Give the form a name and, if you like, a folder.
The builder opens: add questions from the field list on the left.
When you are happy, click **Publish** and share the link.

blocks.text: Not sure where to start? The AI assistant can draft the whole form from a few words: open **AI assistant → Create a form**.

blocks.text: Everyone in your workspace has a profile with their department, job title and role. The role decides what they can see and do.

blocks.caption: People: everyone in your workspace, with Add user and Sign-up links at the top.

items: Open **People** from the rail.
Click **Add user** to create a profile: the person gets an email to set their password.
Or open **Sign-up links** to share a link: people who sign up with it wait for your approval.

keyboard-and-search.summary: Find anything with Ctrl + K and move around with the keyboard.

blocks.text: Search opens with **Ctrl + K** (**⌘ + K** on a Mac). Type part of a page, form, setting or person and press Enter.

blocks.caption: Every keyboard shortcut, in Help & support → Keyboard shortcuts.

blocks.text: Press **?** to see every keyboard shortcut. Many pages add their own, for example **J** and **K** to move between responses in a panel.
Every list and panel works with the keyboard alone: Tab moves, Enter opens, Esc closes.

forms-list.title: Find and organise your forms
forms-list.summary: Search, filter, sort and switch between table and cards.

blocks.text: The Forms page lists every form you may see. The two cards at the top show recent responses and how your forms are spread across draft, published and closed; click a status in the legend to show only those forms.

blocks.caption: Forms as cards, with search, filters and the Table / Grid switch.

items: **Search** by name, tag or owner.
**Filter** by status, folder, owner or tag; filters show as chips you can clear.
**Columns** lets you show, hide and reorder the table’s columns.
**Table / Grid** switches between rows and cards; Formalie remembers your choice.
Right-click a form, or use its **⋯** menu, for actions such as duplicate, move or archive.

form-lifecycle.title: Draft, published, closed and archived
form-lifecycle.summary: What each status means and how a form moves between them.

items: **Draft**: being built; nobody can fill it in yet.
**Published**: open for responses at its link.
**Closed**: the link still works but shows that the form is closed; no new responses.
**Archived**: put away; hidden from the main list, responses kept.

blocks.text: A published form can have **unpublished changes**: your edits stay in the draft until you publish again, so respondents never see a half-finished change.

blocks.caption: Forms filtered to Published: click a status in the card at the top to filter.

blocks.text: Set opening and closing dates in **Share → Availability** so a form opens and closes by itself.

folders.summary: Group forms in folders and keep some folders to certain people.

blocks.text: Folders group forms, for example by team or project. Create one with **+** next to Folders in the menu, then move forms into it from their **⋯** menu.

blocks.caption: Folders, with the number of forms and responses in each.

blocks.text: Admins can limit a folder to some roles, departments or people with **Folder access**. Everyone else doesn’t see the folder, its forms or their responses anywhere, not even in search or exports.

trash.title: Delete and restore forms
trash.summary: Deleted forms stay in the trash for 30 days.

blocks.text: When you delete a form it goes to **Trash** for 30 days, with its responses. You can restore it from there at any time in those 30 days.

blocks.caption: Trash: deleted forms stay here for 30 days.

blocks.text: **Delete forever** in the trash removes the form and all its responses for good. It can’t be undone.

builder-basics.title: Build a form
builder-basics.summary: Add questions, arrange them in rows and pages, and change their settings.

blocks.text: The builder has three parts: the **field list** on the left, the **form** in the middle and the **settings** of what you selected on the right.

blocks.caption: The builder: the field list, the form and the settings of what you selected.

items: Drag a field from the list onto the form, or click it to add it after the selected field.
Click a field to change its question, help text, whether it’s required, and more.
Put fields side by side by dropping them next to each other; use **Width** to size them.
Add pages with **Add page** to split a long form.
Your changes save as you work; **Undo** and **Redo** are at the top.

blocks.text: No mouse? Select a field and use **Alt + ↑ / ↓** to move it, **Ctrl + D** to duplicate and **Delete** to remove.
The **Assistant** button in the builder suggests missing questions, writes help texts and checks your form.

field-types.title: Which field to use
field-types.summary: The kinds of questions Formalie offers and when to use each.

items: **Text**: short and long answers, email, phone, number, amount, full name.
**Dates**: date, time, date and time, date range, duration.
**Choices**: dropdown, radio, checkboxes, yes / no, ranking, matrix, agreement.
**Ratings**: stars, a 0 to 10 scale, a slider.
**Files**: file upload, photo upload, signature.
**Location**: address, country, language, time zone.
**Advanced**: hidden values and calculations.
**Layout**: section headings, text, images and dividers.

blocks.text: Pick the most specific field: an email field checks the address as people type, a date field shows a calendar, a phone field checks the number.

blocks.caption: The field list groups every kind of question: text, dates, choices, ratings, files and more.

blocks.text: Long lists of choices (countries, departments) work best as a **List Option**, kept once and used in many forms.

builder-logic.title: Show the right questions with logic
builder-logic.summary: Show, hide, require or skip questions depending on earlier answers.

blocks.text: Logic rules change the form while people fill it in: show a follow-up only after a yes, require a phone number for urgent requests, or jump to the end.

blocks.caption: The Logic tab: each rule says When something is answered, Then what happens.

items: Open the **Logic** tab of the form.
Click **Add rule** and choose **When**: a question, a condition and a value.
Choose **Then**: show, hide, require, set a value or jump to a page.
Add more conditions with **and** / **or** if needed.

blocks.text: A question that a rule hides is never required, so people can always send the form.

related.summary: Add questions, arrange them in rows and pages, and change their settings.

calculations.title: Totals and scores with calculations
calculations.summary: Work out totals, averages and scores from the answers.

blocks.text: A **Calculation** field works out a value from other answers, for example quantity × price, an average rating or a risk score. People see the result as they fill in the form.

blocks.caption: A form in the builder; a Calculation field works out its value from other answers.

blocks.text: Write the formula with the questions’ keys in braces, for example **{quantity} * {unit_price}**. Choices can carry a score so they can be added up.

publish-and-versions.summary: Every publish is kept as a version you can compare and restore.

blocks.text: **Publish** makes your draft the live form. Each publish is saved as a numbered version with an optional note about what changed.

blocks.caption: Versions: every publish, ready to compare or restore.

blocks.text: In **Versions** you can compare any version with the draft and restore an older one into the draft.
The Publish button is greyed out when there is nothing new to publish.

blocks.caption: The Design tab with the live preview.

items: Start from a ready **starting point**, then adjust.
Change colours, fonts, the size of fields and buttons.
Add your logo, a cover image or a coloured band at the top.

blocks.text: Save a design as a **theme** to use it on other forms in one click.

blocks.text: A landing page is the page your form sits on: a banner with the title, an introduction, how long it takes and your organisation. Pick one in the designer or keep your own in **Landing pages**.

blocks.caption: Landing pages: the page a form sits on.

related.title: Design how a form looks
related.summary: Colours, fonts, layout, header and thank-you page.

use-a-template.title: Start from a template
use-a-template.summary: Ready forms for many uses, in your language.

blocks.text: The template gallery has ready forms for HR, health and safety, events, sales and more. Each one comes with its questions, logic, calculations and a matching design.

blocks.caption: The template gallery, by category.

items: Open **Templates** from the menu.
Browse by category or search.
Open a template to try it in the preview.
Click **Use template**: a new draft form opens in the builder.

related.title: Make your own templates
related.summary: Save a form as a template for your workspace.

related.title: Create your first form
related.summary: From a blank page, a template or a description, in a few minutes.

save-as-template.title: Make your own templates
save-as-template.summary: Save a form as a template for your workspace.

blocks.text: Any form can become a template for your workspace: open its **⋯** menu and choose **Save as template**. Give it a name, a description and a category. Your templates appear under **Your templates**.

blocks.caption: Your templates appear in the gallery next to Formalie’s.

related.title: Start from a template
related.summary: Ready forms for many uses, in your language.

share-a-form.title: Share a form
share-a-form.summary: Link, QR code, email invitations and short links.

blocks.text: Open the **Share** tab of a published form. From there you can copy its link, download a QR code, create a short link or send email invitations.

blocks.caption: The Share tab: where people can answer and who can open the form.

items: **Link**: copy it and paste it anywhere.
**Custom link**: choose a readable address.
**QR code**: for posters and printed material.
**Invitations**: email people a personal link and see who has responded.

related.title: Who can fill in a form, and when
related.summary: Open to anyone, with a password, invite only, or your organisation.

related.title: Put a form on your website
related.summary: Embed the form in your own pages.

who-can-fill-in.title: Who can fill in a form, and when
who-can-fill-in.summary: Open to anyone, with a password, invite only, or your organisation.

items: **Anyone with the link**.
**With a password** you give out.
**Invite only**: only people you invited by email.
**Your organisation**: people signed in to your workspace.

blocks.text: In **Availability** you can open and close the form on set dates and stop it after a number of responses.

blocks.caption: Who can fill in the form and when, in its Share settings.

related.title: Share a form
related.summary: Link, QR code, email invitations and short links.

embed-a-form.title: Put a form on your website
embed-a-form.summary: Embed the form in your own pages.

blocks.text: In **Share → Embed** copy the code and paste it into your website. You can limit which websites may show the form.

blocks.caption: Embedding and allowed websites are in the Share tab too.

related.title: Share a form
related.summary: Link, QR code, email invitations and short links.

form-languages.title: Forms in several languages
form-languages.summary: Offer a form in more languages; people switch at the top.

blocks.text: A form has a main language and can offer more. In the builder, open the form settings, add a language under **More languages** and translate each text side by side.

blocks.caption: Form settings in the builder, where you add more languages.

blocks.text: **Translate the rest with AI** fills in what is still to do; you check every text before publishing.

responses-basics.title: See your responses
responses-basics.summary: Every answer, per form or across all forms.

blocks.text: **Responses** lists your forms with their responses. Open a form to see its responses as a table or as cards; open a response to see every answer in a panel.

blocks.caption: A form’s responses, with the cards at the top and the list below.

items: Use **J** and **K** to move to the next or previous response.
Filter by status, date, channel or answer.
**Insights** shows a summary per question: choices, averages and the latest text answers.

related.title: Review responses
related.summary: Statuses, tags and notes to work through what comes in.

related.title: Export responses
related.summary: Download responses as a spreadsheet or file.

review-responses.title: Review responses
review-responses.summary: Statuses, tags and notes to work through what comes in.

blocks.text: Each response has a status: **New**, **Reviewed**, **Approved** or **Rejected**. Change it with one click at the top of the response panel.

blocks.caption: A response open in its panel: the status bar at the top, tags and notes below.

blocks.text: Add tags and notes to keep track. Correcting answers is a separate permission, so your role may let you review without changing what people wrote.

related.title: See your responses
related.summary: Every answer, per form or across all forms.

export-responses.title: Export responses
export-responses.summary: Download responses as a spreadsheet or file.

blocks.text: Click **Export** on a form’s responses, choose the format and what to include. Large exports are prepared in the background; you see their progress in **Exports** and get a message when the file is ready.

blocks.caption: Exports: files being prepared and ready to download.

related.title: See your responses
related.summary: Every answer, per form or across all forms.

analytics.title: How your forms perform
analytics.summary: Views, starts, completions and where people stop.

blocks.text: **Analytics** shows how many people opened, started and completed each form, how long it takes and where people stop. Open a form to see each page and question.

blocks.caption: Analytics: views, starts, completions and where people stop.

blocks.text: A question where many people stop is often unclear or asks too much. Try a shorter question or make it optional.

related.title: See your responses
related.summary: Every answer, per form or across all forms.

related.title: Analyse responses with the assistant
related.summary: Themes, tone and questions in plain words.

lists-basics.title: List Option: keep choices once
lists-basics.summary: Lists of choices you use in many forms, with levels.

blocks.text: A **List Option** holds choices you use in many forms, for example departments, products or countries. Change the list once and every form that uses it follows.

blocks.caption: List Option: lists of choices used in many forms.

blocks.text: Lists can have **levels**: pick a country, then only its regions show, then its cities. Very large lists stay on the server and load as people type.
Lists marked **Formalie** are provided for every workspace; you can use them but not change them.

data-sources-basics.title: Store responses in your own database
data-sources-basics.summary: Connect a database and send a form’s responses to it.

blocks.text: **Data sources** connects Formalie to your own databases. Responses can then be stored there too, in tables Formalie creates and keeps in step with the form.

items: Open **Data sources** from the rail and click **Add connection**.
Choose the database type and enter its details; **Test now** checks it works.
In a form’s **Response storage**, choose the connection: new responses are stored there.

database-explorer.summary: Browse tables and run queries without leaving Formalie.

api-basics.summary: Your own endpoints for other systems to read and send data.

blocks.text: The **API service** gives other systems their own endpoints: read responses, send new ones, or look up list options. Each service groups endpoints and has its own documentation page.

blocks.caption: API services, each with its endpoints and documentation.

items: Open **API service** and create a service.
Add endpoints for the forms or data you want to offer.
Create a **token** for the system that will call it.

api-tokens.title: Tokens and access rules
api-tokens.summary: Who may call your endpoints, from where and how often.

blocks.text: Each system that calls your API gets a **token**. Tokens can expire and be revoked at any time. **Access rules** limit addresses, times and how many calls are allowed.

blocks.caption: Tokens & headers: the keys systems use to call your API.

blocks.text: A token is shown once. Keep it in a safe place and never put it in a public web page.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.summary: Tell another system the moment something happens.

blocks.text: A webhook sends a message to another system’s address when something happens, for example a new response. Formalie retries failed deliveries and shows each delivery so you can see what was sent.

blocks.caption: Webhooks and their deliveries.

related.title: The API service

roles-and-access.title: Roles and access
roles-and-access.summary: Decide exactly what each role may see and do.

blocks.caption: Roles & access: each role and who holds it.

blocks.text: Each action has a reach: **None**, **Own** (what they made), **Shared** (forms shared with them), **Own & shared** or **All**. For example, a role may see all responses but only change its own forms.

related.title: Bring in your team

faqs.question: Do people need an account to fill in a form?
faqs.answer: No. Anyone with the link can fill in a form, unless you limit it to invited people, a password or your organisation.

faqs.question: Does Formalie work on phones?
faqs.answer: Yes. Forms and the portal work on phones, tablets and computers.

faqs.question: Which languages does Formalie speak?
faqs.answer: The portal and forms work in 20 languages, including right-to-left languages such as Arabic. Each person chooses their own language in their profile.

faqs.question: Can I change a form that is already published?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your changes stay in the draft until you publish again, so people filling it in never see a half-finished change.

faqs.question: I deleted a form by mistake. Can I get it back?
faqs.answer: Yes, from the Trash, within 30 days, with its responses.

faqs.question: How do I copy a form?
faqs.answer: Open its ⋯ menu and choose Duplicate. The copy is a new draft with the same questions and design.

faqs.question: How do I make a question required?
faqs.answer: Select it in the builder and switch on Required in its settings.

faqs.question: How do I split a form into pages?
faqs.answer: Click Add page in the builder and move questions to it.

faqs.question: Can a question only show after a certain answer?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a logic rule: When the earlier question has that answer, Then show the follow-up.

faqs.question: How do I add our logo?
faqs.answer: Add it once in Settings → Branding; forms show it in their header. You can also set it per form in Design.

faqs.question: Can we make our own templates?
faqs.answer: Yes. Save any form as a template from its ⋯ menu.

faqs.question: Can a form close by itself?
faqs.answer: Yes. Set a closing date or a maximum number of responses in Share → Availability.

faqs.question: How do I get a QR code?
faqs.answer: In the form’s Share tab, download the QR code as an image.

faqs.question: Can I get an email for each new response?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose who is emailed in the form’s settings, and set your own notifications in Settings → Notifications.

faqs.question: Which formats can I export?
faqs.answer: Spreadsheets and other file formats; choose in the export dialog.

faqs.question: Can I correct an answer someone gave?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your role allows correcting answers. The change is recorded in the audit trail.

faqs.question: Where do people stop filling in my form?
faqs.answer: Open the form in Analytics: it shows each page and question with how many people left there.

faqs.question: If I change a list, do my forms change too?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every form that uses the list follows it.

faqs.question: Can responses go straight to our own database?
faqs.answer: Yes. Connect it in Data sources and choose it in the form’s Response storage.

faqs.question: I lost my API token. What now?
faqs.answer: Tokens are shown once. Revoke the lost one and create a new token.

faqs.question: Can we make our own roles?
faqs.answer: Yes. In People → Roles & access, add a role and choose what it may do and how far it reaches.

faqs.question: Someone left. How do I remove their access?
faqs.answer: Open them in People and choose Disable. They are signed out at once; their forms and responses stay.

faqs.question: I forgot my password.
faqs.answer: Click Forgot password on the sign-in page; you get a code by email to set a new one.

faqs.question: I lost the phone with my authenticator app.
faqs.answer: Sign in with one of your recovery codes, or ask an admin to reset your two-step sign-in.

faqs.question: How do I see who changed a form?
faqs.answer: Open the audit trail and filter by the form or by Forms; each entry shows who, when and what changed.

faqs.question: Does the AI assistant learn from our data?
faqs.answer: No. Requests are only used to answer them and are kept only for the time set in AI settings.

faqs.question: What are AI credits?
faqs.answer: Each request uses a few credits from your workspace’s monthly allowance. See them in AI assistant → Settings & usage.

faqs.question: Can we switch the assistant off?
faqs.answer: Yes. Admins switch it off in AI assistant → Settings & usage; nothing is sent to it while it is off.

glossary.definition: The unit the AI assistant’s monthly allowance is counted in; each request uses a few.
The record of every action in your workspace: who, what, when and where.
A field that works out a value, such as a total or score, from other answers.
A connection to one of your databases, used to store responses and explore data.
The version of a form you are working on. People only see it once you publish.
Showing a form inside your own website.
An address in your API service that another system calls to read or send data.
One question or block in a form, such as a text box, a choice or a signature.
A group of forms. Admins can limit who sees a folder.
A set of questions people fill in, with its design, logic and settings.
The short name of a question (like first_name), used in formulas, exports and the API.
A list of choices kept once and used in many forms; changes reach every form using it.
A list where a choice decides the next one, such as country, then region, then city.
A rule that shows, hides, requires or skips questions depending on answers.
How far a permission goes: only what the person made, what was shared with them, or everything.
One person’s filled-in form, with all their answers.
A set of permissions given to people, deciding what they can see and do.
A ready form you start from, with questions, logic and design.
A saved design: colours, fonts and layout you can use on any form.
A secret key a system uses to call your API. Shown once; can expire or be revoked.
A code asked for after your password, from an app, email or text message.
A published state of a form, kept so you can compare and restore it.
A message Formalie sends to another system the moment something happens.
Your organisation’s own space in Formalie, at its own address, with its people, forms and settings.

article.title: Delete and restore forms
article.summary: Deleted forms stay in the trash for 30 days.

blocks.text: When you delete a form it goes to **Trash** for 30 days, with its responses. You can restore it from there at any time in those 30 days.

blocks.caption: Trash: deleted forms stay here for 30 days.

blocks.text: **Delete forever** in the trash removes the form and all its responses for good. It can’t be undone.

items: Drag a field from the list onto the form, or click it to add it after the selected field.

blocks.text: No mouse? Select a field and use **Alt + ↑ / ↓** to move it, **Ctrl + D** to duplicate and **Delete** to remove.

article.title: Show the right questions with logic

blocks.text: Logic rules change the form while people fill it in: show a follow-up only after a yes, require a phone number for urgent requests, or jump to the end.

blocks.caption: The Logic tab: each rule says When something is answered, Then what happens.

items: Open the **Logic** tab of the form.
Click **Add rule** and choose **When**: a question, a condition and a value.
Choose **Then**: show, hide, require, set a value or jump to a page.
Add more conditions with **and** / **or** if needed.

blocks.text: A question that a rule hides is never required, so people can always send the form.

blocks.text: Each action has a reach: **None**, **Own** (what they made), **Shared** (forms shared with them), **Own & shared** or **All**. For example, a role may see all responses but only change its own forms.

blocks.text: Click **Export** on a form’s responses, choose the format and what to include. Large exports are prepared in the background; you see their progress in **Exports** and get a message when the file is ready.

articles: A webhook sends a message to another system’s address when something happens, for example a new response.

blocks.text: A webhook sends a message to another system’s address when something happens, for example a new response. Formalie retries failed deliveries and shows each delivery so you can see what was sent.

articles: The API service gives other systems their own endpoints: read responses, send new ones, or look up list options.
Each system that calls your API gets a token.

blocks.text: The **API service** gives other systems their own endpoints: read responses, send new ones, or look up list options. Each service groups endpoints and has its own documentation page.

articles: Two-step sign-in asks for a code after your password.

blocks.text: Two-step sign-in asks for a code after your password. Set up an authenticator app in your profile for the safest option, and keep the recovery codes somewhere safe.

articles: Your templates appear under Your templates.

blocks.text: When you delete a form it goes to **Trash** for 30 days, with its responses. You can restore it from there at any time in those 30 days.

articles: تساعد Formalie مؤسستك على جمع المعلومات بالنماذج، ومراجعة ما يصلها، وإرساله إلى حيث تحتاجه: قاعدة بيانات، أو نظام آخر عبر API، أو تقرير.

blocks.text: تساعد Formalie مؤسستك على جمع المعلومات بالنماذج، ومراجعة ما يصلها، وإرساله إلى حيث تحتاجه: قاعدة بيانات، أو نظام آخر عبر API، أو تقرير.

articles: العمود الضيق على جانب الشاشة هو شريط الأيقونات.

blocks.text: العمود الضيق على جانب الشاشة هو **شريط الأيقونات**. كل أيقونة تفتح قسمًا من Formalie: النماذج، مصادر البيانات، خدمة API، مساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي والأشخاص. وتتغير القائمة المجاورة بحسب القسم الذي تكون فيه.

articles: يمكنك بدء نموذج بثلاث طرق: من صفحة فارغة، أو من أحد قوالب Formalie، أو بوصفه لمساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي.
للمُنشئ ثلاثة أجزاء: قائمة الحقول على جانب، والنموذج في الوسط، وإعدادات ما حددته على الجانب الآخر.
افتح مساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي → إنشاء نموذج.
المالك يستطيع كل شيء؛ والمسؤول والعضو جاهزان للاستخدام ويمكن تغييرهما؛ ويمكنك إضافة أدوارك الخاصة.
يشغّل المسؤولون المساعد أو يوقفونه، ويحددون ما يقرؤه (النماذج، الردود، مصادر البيانات)، ويستبعدون البيانات الشخصية، ويحددون مدة الاحتفاظ بالطلبات.

blocks.text: يمكنك بدء نموذج بثلاث طرق: من صفحة فارغة، أو من أحد قوالب Formalie، أو بوصفه لمساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي.

articles: أضف زملاءك بملف شخصي، أو شارك رابط تسجيل.

blocks.text: لكل شخص في مساحة عملك ملف شخصي يتضمن قسمه ومسماه الوظيفي ودوره. والدور هو الذي يحدد ما يستطيع رؤيته وفعله.

articles: اعثر على أي شيء بـ Ctrl + K وتنقّل بلوحة المفاتيح.

blocks.text: يُفتح البحث بـ **Ctrl + K** (**⌘ + K** على ماك). اكتب جزءًا من اسم صفحة أو نموذج أو إعداد أو شخص ثم اضغط Enter.

articles: تعرض البطاقتان في الأعلى الردود الأخيرة وكيف تتوزع نماذجك بين مسودة ومنشور ومغلق؛ اضغط على حالة في مفتاح الرسم لعرض تلك النماذج فقط.

blocks.text: تعرض صفحة النماذج كل نموذج يحق لك رؤيته. تعرض البطاقتان في الأعلى الردود الأخيرة وكيف تتوزع نماذجك بين مسودة ومنشور ومغلق؛ اضغط على حالة في مفتاح الرسم لعرض تلك النماذج فقط.

articles: مسودة: قيد الإنشاء؛ لا يستطيع أحد ملأه بعد.

blocks.text: قد يحتوي النموذج المنشور على **تغييرات غير منشورة**: تبقى تعديلاتك في المسودة حتى تنشر مرة أخرى، فلا يرى المجيبون تغييرًا نصف مكتمل.

articles: تجمع المجلدات النماذج، مثلًا بحسب الفريق أو المشروع.

blocks.text: تجمع المجلدات النماذج، مثلًا بحسب الفريق أو المشروع. أنشئ مجلدًا بالزر **+** بجانب المجلدات في القائمة، ثم انقل النماذج إليه من قائمة **⋯** الخاصة بها.

articles: عند حذف نموذج ينتقل إلى سلة المهملات 30 يومًا مع ردوده.

blocks.text: عند حذف نموذج ينتقل إلى **سلة المهملات** 30 يومًا مع ردوده. ويمكنك استعادته من هناك في أي وقت خلال هذه الأيام الـ 30.

articles: إنشاء نموذج: صِف النموذج على اليمين، والمسودة ومعاينتها على اليسار.
يمكنك بدء نموذج بثلاث طرق: من صفحة فارغة، أو من أحد قوالب Formalie، أو بوصفه لمساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي.
للمُنشئ ثلاثة أجزاء: قائمة الحقول على جانب، والنموذج في الوسط، وإعدادات ما حددته على الجانب الآخر.
يمكن لأي نموذج أن يصبح قالبًا لمساحة عملك: افتح قائمة ⋯ الخاصة به واختر حفظ كقالب.
تحدد الإعدادات الافتراضية للنماذج السمة وشريط التقدم والتسميات ورسالة الشكر والرسائل الإلكترونية التي يبدأ بها كل نموذج جديد.
اختر الحقل الأكثر تحديدًا: حقل البريد الإلكتروني يتحقق من العنوان أثناء الكتابة، وحقل التاريخ يعرض تقويمًا، وحقل الهاتف يتحقق من الرقم.

blocks.text: اختر الحقل الأكثر تحديدًا: حقل البريد الإلكتروني يتحقق من العنوان أثناء الكتابة، وحقل التاريخ يعرض تقويمًا، وحقل الهاتف يتحقق من الرقم.

articles: تغيّر قواعد المنطق النموذج أثناء ملئه: أظهر سؤال متابعة بعد الإجابة بنعم فقط، أو اشترط رقم هاتف للطلبات العاجلة، أو اقفز إلى النهاية.

blocks.text: تغيّر قواعد المنطق النموذج أثناء ملئه: أظهر سؤال متابعة بعد الإجابة بنعم فقط، أو اشترط رقم هاتف للطلبات العاجلة، أو اقفز إلى النهاية.

articles: يحسب حقل العملية الحسابية قيمة من إجابات أخرى، مثل الكمية × السعر أو متوسط تقييم أو درجة مخاطر.

blocks.text: يحسب حقل **العملية الحسابية** قيمة من إجابات أخرى، مثل الكمية × السعر أو متوسط تقييم أو درجة مخاطر. ويرى الناس النتيجة أثناء ملء النموذج.

articles: النشر يجعل مسودتك هي النموذج الفعلي.

blocks.text: **النشر** يجعل مسودتك هي النموذج الفعلي. ويُحفظ كل نشر كإصدار مرقّم مع ملاحظة اختيارية عمّا تغيّر.

articles: افتح تبويب التصميم في النموذج لتغيير مظهره.

blocks.text: افتح تبويب **التصميم** في النموذج لتغيير مظهره. وتعرض المعاينة النموذج كما سيراه الناس على حاسوب أو جهاز لوحي أو هاتف.
السمات هي تصاميم محفوظة. تأتي Formalie بمجموعة منها؛ ويمكن لمساحة عملك إضافة سماتها من المصمّم، أو أن يقترح مساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي تصاميم من لون علامتك.

articles: ما الذي تفعله Formalie وكيف تُرتَّب البوابة.

blocks.text: تساعد Formalie مؤسستك على جمع المعلومات بالنماذج، ومراجعة ما يصلها، وإرساله إلى حيث تحتاجه: قاعدة بيانات، أو نظام آخر عبر API، أو تقرير.

articles: تحتفظ قائمة الخيارات بخيارات تستخدمها في نماذج كثيرة، مثل الأقسام أو المنتجات أو الدول.
كل أيقونة تفتح قسمًا من Formalie: النماذج، مصادر البيانات، خدمة API، مساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي والأشخاص.
اضغط بزر الفأرة الأيمن على نموذج، أو استخدم قائمة ⋯ الخاصة به، لإجراءات مثل التكرار أو النقل أو الأرشفة.
في الإعدادات → الأمان يضع المسؤولون قواعد كلمة المرور ويشترطون تسجيل الدخول بخطوتين ويحددون مدة بقاء الناس مسجَّلين، ويسمحون عند الحاجة بتسجيل الدخول من شبكاتك فقط.

blocks.text: تحتفظ **قائمة الخيارات** بخيارات تستخدمها في نماذج كثيرة، مثل الأقسام أو المنتجات أو الدول. غيّر القائمة مرة واحدة فيتبعها كل نموذج يستخدمها.

articles: لست متأكدًا من أين تبدأ؟ يستطيع مساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي صياغة النموذج كاملًا من بضع كلمات: افتح مساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي → إنشاء نموذج.

blocks.text: **Formularstandards** legt Design, Fortschrittsbalken, Beschriftungen, Dankesnachricht und E-Mails fest, mit denen jedes neue Formular beginnt. Bestehende Formulare ändern sich nicht.
